questions.stem_latex:
A bag contains 2 white and 5 yellow tokens.

In a group of people, each person draws a token randomly from the bag, with replacement.

If the token is white, they answer the question “Are you a smoker?”

If a yellow token is drawn, they answer the question “Are you a non-smoker?”

They then answer either “Yes” or “No”, depending on whether they smoke or not.

Let $p$ be the probability that a randomly selected person is a smoker.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Show that the probability that a randomly selected person answered “Yes” is given by:

$$P(\text{Yes})=\dfrac{5-3p}{7}.$$

parts.label: b
parts.latex: It is now known that the group has 91 people and 50 of them answered “Yes”.

parts.label: i
parts.latex: Find $p$.

parts.label: ii
parts.latex: Given a person answered “No”, find the probability that they are a non-smoker.

Brendan eats $1,3,5,\dots$ which is an AP with $a=1$, $d=2$, so $T_n=1+2(n-1)$.

He can eat a maximum of $3000\div 0.5=6000$ in total.

$$S_n=6000=\dfrac{n}{2}\left(2\times 1+2(n-1)\right)=n^2$$

$n=\sqrt{6000}=77.45$ $(n>0)$.

Therefore the game ends in 77 rounds, as Brendan can’t fit in the next round.

$T_{77}=1+2(77-1)=153$.

Consider $1+\sin^2x+\sin^4x+\sin^6x+\dots$, a GP with $a=1$, $r=\sin^2x$. Since $x\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $|r|<1$.

$$S_\infty=\dfrac{1}{1-\sin^2x}=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2x}=\sec^2x$$

$\therefore\ \sqrt{S_\infty}=\sqrt{\sec^2x}=\sec x$, since $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}<x<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ gives $\sec x>0$.

$$\begin{aligned}\int_2^{14}\dfrac{60t}{1+5t}\,dt&=12\left[t-\dfrac{1}{5}\ln(1+5t)\right]_2^{14}\\&=12\left[14-\dfrac{1}{5}\ln(1+5\times 14)-\left(2-\dfrac{1}{5}\ln(1+5\times 2)\right)\right]\\&=12\left[12-\dfrac{1}{5}\ln\left(\dfrac{71}{11}\right)\right]\approx 139.52\end{aligned}$$

Therefore company $B$ will produce approximately 139.52 hundred barrels. From part (a), company $A$ produced approximately 138.25 hundred barrels.

So from these estimates, Company $B$ is producing more. However, the estimate for Company $A$ was obtained using the trapezoidal rule. As the natural log function is concave down, this will be an underestimate and the values are very close. So it is not possible to say from these values which company produces more oil over that period.
